sources.title: Cabo Verde Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Current and historical exposure; climate scenarios through 2050 and 2100; cited social data years vary by indicator.
sources.methodology: CCDR uses geospatial exposure analysis and climate scenarios.
sources.limitations: Modeled estimates depend on stated thresholds and cited data years.

sources.title: Cape Verde Floods: Operation Update #1 (MDRCV005)
sources.organization: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
sources.temporal_coverage: August 2025 floods and IFRC/Cabo Verde Red Cross response reported through 30 September 2025.
sources.methodology: IFRC operation update reports crisis effects, local needs and response outputs for August–September 2025.
sources.limitations: Operational figures and response outputs are not an independent post-disaster evaluation.

sources.title: Cabo Verde launches national roll-out of Early Warnings for All
sources.temporal_coverage: National Early Warnings for All rollout and draft roadmap announced in December 2025.
sources.methodology: WMO update summarizing a national rollout and multi-stakeholder workshop.
sources.limitations: The roadmap was still awaiting validation; no warning-system performance results are reported.

sources.title: Building Adaptive Capacity and Resilience to Climate Change in the Water Sector in Cabo Verde
sources.temporal_coverage: Completed UNDP/GEF water-sector adaptation project; page gives no project completion date.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describes intervention design, pilot locations and reported completion status.
sources.limitations: Page does not name all municipalities or independently quantify adaptation outcomes.

sources.title: Governo anuncia plano de emergência para mitigação da seca e mau ano agrícola
sources.temporal_coverage: Government announcement of the 2017–2018 drought and poor agricultural-year emergency program.
sources.methodology: Government announcement describing program scope, intended beneficiaries and implementation arrangements.
sources.limitations: The announcement records approved measures, not delivery or effectiveness results.

claims.locator: PDF p. 30 (printed p. 18), section 1.3 and figures 1.15–1.16
claims.paraphrase: Estimated: 16% exposed to extreme drought, 7% to extreme floods; poor households face 1.4x drought exposure. Drought affects all islands (lower in São Vicente/Sal); 90% of flood exposure is in Santiago/Santo Antão.
claims.limitations: Modeled 40-year drought and 100-year flood thresholds, not past-event counts.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 46–47 (printed pp. 34–35), section 3.2, food-security hotspots and figure 3.7
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR identifies 143,000 people (28%) in poverty/food-insecurity hotspots; six municipalities have acute food insecurity of at least 15%, five on Santiago and one on Santo Antão.
claims.limitations: Municipal poverty categories use island-level poverty data, not municipal poverty estimates.

claims.locator: PDF p. 54 (printed p. 42), section 3.4 and figure 3.8
claims.paraphrase: RCP 8.5 projections raise coastal-flood exposure from 29% of coastal residents now to about 32% by 2050; Sal's exposed urban coast could rise from 33% to over 38%.
claims.limitations: Modelled exposure; island-level variation is substantial.

claims.locator: PDF p. 54 (printed p. 42), section 3.4, rural-to-urban migration and city exposure
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR identifies drought and tourism as rural-to-urban migration drivers, especially toward Sal and Boa Vista.
claims.limitations: No causal estimate or conflict attribution is provided.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The CCDR links drought to migration, not conflict or violence.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 2–3, crisis description and needs assessment, August 2025 floods
claims.paraphrase: The IFRC update reports at least 12 deaths, five missing, over 27,500 affected and 1,500 displaced in São Vicente after floods and landslides, with damage to homes, roads, health services, markets and water systems.
claims.limitations: Emergency-operation figures for a defined period; they are not an independent damage survey.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: IFRC links flood displacement, income loss and reduced assistance access to heightened protection risks for vulnerable groups; it does not claim conflict causation.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 4–5 and 11, shelter/food assistance and protection, gender and inclusion sections
claims.paraphrase: By September 2025, the Red Cross had provided household items to 238 households and food to 271 in named São Vicente neighborhoods, and conducted three protection and inclusion trainings for 79 volunteers.
claims.limitations: The update reports ongoing delivery; post-distribution monitoring was still planned.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, host National Society response overview
claims.paraphrase: The Red Cross reports ferrying about 150 m³ of drinking water daily from Santo Antão to São Vicente after flooding damaged the local distribution system.
claims.limitations: Short-term emergency supply; the update does not document long-term network restoration.

claims.locator: WMO update paragraphs 27–58, national rollout and roadmap
claims.paraphrase: WMO reports Cabo Verde launched Early Warnings for All in December 2025; a five-year roadmap was drafted with national institutional leads, with validation and implementation expected in 2026.
affected_groups: people exposed to weather and climate hazards
institutions: National Institute of Meteorology and Geophysics
claims.limitations: Launch and roadmap milestones do not establish operational coverage or warning effectiveness.

claims.locator: UNDP project summary and pilot activities, lines 62–75
claims.paraphrase: UNDP's completed-project page describes pilots across three municipalities and five basins, including groundwater intake and drip irrigation in Ribeira Seca and planned reforestation/soil conservation at Planalto Leste on Santo Antão.
affected_groups: communities dependent on local water resources
claims.limitations: The page does not name every municipality or independently verify adaptation outcomes.

claims.locator: Government article paragraphs 40–46, 2017–2018 drought emergency plan
claims.paraphrase: For the 2017–2018 drought and poor agricultural year, the government announced an 880,000-contos program for livestock rescue, water-scarcity management and family employment, aimed at rural farm productivity, income and food-security losses.
claims.limitations: Government announcement of approved measures, not evidence of delivery or effectiveness.

search_audit.query: Cabo Verde drought flood exposure island municipality food insecurity coastal flooding CCDR local vulnerability
search_audit.outcome: The full CCDR provides modeled island-level drought/flood exposure, coastal flood estimates and municipality-level food-insecurity hotspots; IFRC reports 2025 flood damage and response in named São Vicente neighborhoods.

search_audit.query: Cabo Verde climate drought migration displacement violence conflict protection risk report
search_audit.outcome: The CCDR says drought and tourism have driven rural-to-urban migration; IFRC links flood displacement and reduced assistance access to heightened protection risks. No inspected source attributes violence or conflict to climate hazards.

search_audit.query: Cabo Verde conflict insecurity political instability constraining climate adaptation disaster response
search_audit.outcome: No source-stated evidence was located that conflict or insecurity constrains climate adaptation in Cabo Verde; reviewed climate, disaster and resilience sources discuss service, coordination and coverage constraints instead.

search_audit.query: Cabo Verde local drought response adaptation water resilience early warning flood recovery capacity report
search_audit.outcome: Government announced a drought program; UNDP describes completed water-adaptation project sites; IFRC documents emergency assistance; WMO reports a national early-warning rollout and draft roadmap. Plans and ongoing operations are not treated as evaluated outcomes.

gaps: No inspected source explicitly links climate hazards to armed conflict or violence in Cabo Verde. The CCDR links drought with rural-to-urban migration, and IFRC reports flood displacement and heightened protection risks, without establishing conflict causation.
The CCDR's municipality food-insecurity categories use island-level poverty data; modeled hazard estimates use different return periods and cited data years.
IFRC flood counts are operation-period estimates; response monitoring was incomplete, and the WMO roadmap was still awaiting validation in its December 2025 update.
UNDP's project summary does not name every municipality or independently quantify the adaptation outcomes of its completed project.
